blocks.content: Investments of 10% or more of the post-issue paid-up equity capital of a listed company are classified as Foreign Direct Investment (FDI), whereas investments below 10% are treated as Foreign Portfolio Investment (FPI).

rows: 10% or more of paid-up equity capital
Less than 10% of paid-up equity capital
Long-term strategic interest with physical assets or operational control
Short-term financial returns with passive ownership in securities
Low liquidity; difficult entry and exit process
Brings technological transfer, management expertise, and employment generation
Brings capital flows into stock/bond markets without direct management involvement

items: In Masala Bonds, the exchange rate risk is borne by the investor, whereas in Foreign Currency Convertible Bonds (FCCBs), the currency risk lies with the issuer.
FDI is strictly prohibited in Atomic Energy, Lottery Business, Gambling/Betting, Chit Funds, Nidhi Companies, and Real Estate Business (excluding townships/construction projects).
P-Notes (Participatory Notes) are frequently audited by SEBI to prevent money laundering, round-tripping, and untraceable capital inflows.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) refers to long-term capital investments where the foreign investor holds 10% or more of the post-issue paid-up equity capital of an Indian company.
Foreign Portfolio Investment (FPI) represents short-term passive investments in equity or debt securities holding less than 10% stake, often termed 'hot money' due to its volatile nature.
Masala Bonds are foreign-listed, rupee-denominated bonds that transfer the currency risk entirely from the Indian issuing entity to the foreign investor.
Participatory Notes (P-Notes/ODIs) allow unregistered foreign entities to invest in Indian stock markets through registered Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) under strict SEBI compliance.
The Foreign Investment Facilitation Portal (FIFP) replaced the Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) to administer FDI under the government approval route.
